title: Asking Clarifying Questions in Open-Domain Information-Seeking Conversations
abstract: Studies clarification as a response to incompletely expressed information needs and introduces a framework in which clarifying-question selection precedes document retrieval, making the work directly relevant to detecting and filling missing conversational context.

title: MIMICS: A Large-Scale Data Collection for Search Clarification
abstract: Presents large-scale search-interaction data containing clarifying questions, candidate answers, and user feedback, supporting research on recognizing and resolving underspecified information needs.

title: Query Resolution for Conversational Search with Limited Supervision
abstract: Introduces QuReTeC for resolving underspecified conversational queries by selecting useful terms from dialogue history and shows how the resolved query improves passage retrieval under limited supervision.

title: Open-Retrieval Conversational Question Answering
abstract: Formulates conversational QA without a pre-supplied evidence passage, requiring retrieval from a large corpus before reranking and answer extraction while using conversation history to contextualize the information need.

title: Weakly-Supervised Open-Retrieval Conversational Question Answering
abstract: Develops weak supervision for retrieving conversational evidence when answers can be free-form or paraphrastic, extending open-retrieval conversational QA beyond exact answer-span supervision.

title: Few-Shot Conversational Dense Retrieval
abstract: Introduces ConvDR, which learns contextualized dense representations for conversational retrieval and is designed to retain informative prior context while suppressing irrelevant dialogue history.

title: CONQRR: Conversational Query Rewriting for Retrieval with Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Trains conversational query rewriting directly against retrieval rewards, connecting contextual resolution to whether downstream evidence can actually be retrieved rather than optimizing rewriting alone.

title: ConvGQR: Generative Query Reformulation for Conversational Search
abstract: Combines conversational query rewriting with generation of potential answers and knowledge infusion so that reformulation is explicitly tied to downstream retrieval effectiveness.

title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Introduces active retrieval during generation, including FLARE, which anticipates upcoming content and triggers retrieval when generation confidence indicates that additional external evidence is needed.

title: Self-Knowledge Guided Retrieval Augmentation for Large Language Models
abstract: Uses an estimate of an LLM's own knowledge to determine whether external retrieval should be invoked, avoiding retrieval for questions judged answerable from existing knowledge.

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
abstract: Trains a model to retrieve on demand and emit reflection signals that critique retrieved passages and generated claims, allowing retrieval to be skipped or repeated according to perceived need and support.

title: Adaptive-RAG: Learning to Adapt Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models through Question Complexity
abstract: Routes questions among no-retrieval, single-step retrieval, and iterative retrieval strategies according to predicted question complexity, providing a learned mechanism for varying retrieval effort.

title: DRAGIN: Dynamic Retrieval Augmented Generation based on the Information Needs of Large Language Models
abstract: Models a language model's changing information needs during generation to determine both when retrieval should occur and what query should be issued for the missing information.

title: SeaKR: Self-aware Knowledge Retrieval for Adaptive Retrieval Augmented Generation
abstract: Uses uncertainty in model internal states to trigger retrieval, reranks retrieved knowledge according to uncertainty reduction, and supports repeated retrieval when current evidence remains inadequate.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: Defines and studies whether retrieved context contains enough information to answer a question, develops context-sufficiency classification, and examines selective answering and abstention when evidence is insufficient.

title: Review-Then-Refine: A Dynamic Framework for Multi-Hop Question Answering with Temporal Adaptability
abstract: Uses dynamically refined subqueries and temporal information during multi-hop retrieval, allowing retrieval behavior to respond to accumulated evidence instead of following an unchanged initial query.

title: Know Before You Fetch: Calibrated Retrieval-Budget Allocation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: Formulates adaptive RAG as calibrated allocation among closed-book answering, compact retrieval, larger retrieval, and abstention, explicitly exposing retrieval budget together with latency and token-cost trade-offs.

title: AB-RAG: Adaptive Budgeted Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Reliable Question Answering
abstract: Estimates answer confidence from model certainty, evidence agreement, and retrieval-score variation, then chooses whether to stop or retrieve additional evidence subject to an explicit retrieval budget.

title: S2G-RAG: Structured Sufficiency and Gap Judging for Iterative Retrieval-Augmented QA
abstract: Introduces an explicit controller that judges whether accumulated evidence is sufficient and, when it is not, emits structured descriptions of the missing evidence; those gap items become the next retrieval query, while a compact evidence context limits accumulation of irrelevant text.

title: When Should Multi-Round RAG Stop? Structured Stopping Judgments and Retrieval Reduction in Search-R1
abstract: Treats multi-round retrieval stopping as a sequential decision and applies structured sufficiency-and-gap judgments to decide the first state at which retrieval should terminate rather than relying only on a fixed search budget.

title: AdaKG-RAG: Adaptive KG-guided retrieval-augmented generation with hypothesis-and-verification retrieval for multi-hop question answering
abstract: Uses hypothesis-and-verification retrieval in a closed loop and evaluates evidence sufficiency, support consistency, confidence, and missing evidence to guide subsequent retrieval for multi-hop questions.
venue: Journal of King Saud University Computer and Information Sciences

title: CORAL: Adaptive Retrieval Loop for Culturally-Aligned Multilingual RAG
abstract: Iteratively selects a retrieval corpus, retrieves evidence, critiques its relevance and alignment, checks sufficiency, and, when evidence is insufficient, changes the corpus selection and rewrites the retrieval query.

title: Adaptive iterative retrieval for enhanced retrieval-augmented generation
abstract: Presents AIR-RAG, which feeds model feedback into subsequent retrieval and document refinement so that retrieved context is progressively adjusted to better match the downstream model's information needs.

title: Interleaving Retrieval with Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Knowledge-Intensive Multi-Step Questions
abstract: Introduces IRCoT, which interleaves reasoning and retrieval so later retrieval queries are conditioned on facts and intermediate conclusions obtained earlier in the evidence chain.

title: Measuring and Narrowing the Compositionality Gap in Language Models
abstract: Introduces self-ask, in which a model generates follow-up questions during multi-step reasoning and can send those questions to an external search system, providing a transferable mechanism for deciding the next evidence request.

title: Demonstrate-Search-Predict: Composing retrieval and language models for knowledge-intensive NLP
abstract: Introduces a programming framework that composes language-model transformations, retrieval, and grounded prediction into multi-stage programs, including multi-hop and conversational retrieval workflows.

title: REAP: Enhancing RAG with Recursive Evaluation and Adaptive Planning for Multi-Hop Question Answering
abstract: Uses recursive evaluation and adaptive planning to represent intermediate subtasks and facts, assess the current retrieval state, and alter the retrieval trajectory as evidence accumulates.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Multi-Hop Question Answering Based on Structured Planning
abstract: Introduces structured planning for multi-hop RAG to organize successive retrieval steps and reduce drift and irrelevant evidence during iterative information acquisition.
venue: ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data

title: CIRAG: Construction–Integration Retrieval and Adaptive Generation for Multi-hop Question Answering
abstract: Iteratively constructs and integrates candidate evidence and uses the resulting state to generate subsequent retrieval queries, coupling evidence accumulation with adaptive answer generation.

title: SA-RAG: Structured and adaptive retrieval-augmented generation for multi-hop question answering
abstract: Models evidence in a structured form and learns an adaptive policy over retrieval, search, completion, correction, and answering actions, with objectives that balance answer quality, evidence coverage, and efficiency.

title: Beyond Single-Shot: Multi-step Tool Retrieval via Query Planning
abstract: Models retrieval as iterative query planning, decomposing a complex request into successive retrieval queries rather than treating source selection as a single-shot ranking problem.

title: Selective Question Answering under Domain Shift
abstract: Studies selective QA systems that predict when their answers are likely to be wrong and abstain under distribution shift, providing a transferable basis for distinguishing answerable states from states requiring further evidence.

title: An Initial Investigation into Fixed and Adaptive Stopping Strategies
abstract: Investigates fixed and adaptive stopping strategies in interactive information retrieval, directly addressing how search depth can depend on observed interaction rather than an invariant document-count cutoff.

title: An Analysis of Stopping Strategies in Conversational Search Systems
abstract: Studies stopping points in conversational search and identifies interaction and textual signals that can predict when a searcher terminates a conversational information-seeking process.

title: Online search stopping behaviors: An investigation of query abandonment and task stopping
abstract: Empirically distinguishes abandonment of the current query from termination of the overall search task and examines factors associated with each stopping decision in online information seeking.
venue: Proceedings of the American Society for Information Science and Technology

title: Active Learning Stopping Strategies for Technology-Assisted Sensitivity Review
abstract: Examines stopping strategies for active-learning document review in sensitivity-review workflows, where documents are acquired and assessed sequentially and review effort must be bounded.

title: Decision-Theoretic Stopping Rules for Document Screening
abstract: Derives practical document-screening stopping policies from Expected Value of Perfect Information so that additional evidence is acquired only when its expected benefit justifies its cost for the underlying professional task.

title: The value of information as a verification and regret-preventing mechanism in algorithmic search environments
abstract: Develops an information-acquisition approach based on the value of new information and a stopping criterion tied to the decision maker's current beliefs, offering a decision-theoretic foundation for cost-sensitive evidence acquisition.

title: Time-based language models
abstract: Introduces time into language-model-based retrieval, providing an early foundation for ranking documents according to both topical evidence and temporal characteristics rather than textual similarity alone.

title: Temporal profiles of queries
abstract: Models temporal profiles of queries and retrieved material, supporting retrieval systems that need to reason about how relevance and information demand vary over time.

title: Improving search relevance for implicitly temporal queries
abstract: Addresses queries whose temporal intent is implicit and develops retrieval methods that incorporate temporal evidence when ordinary topical matching does not fully capture the user's information need.

title: Understanding Temporal Query Dynamics
abstract: Analyzes how query popularity, result content, user intent, and relevance change over time, establishing distinctions useful for deciding which temporal state of a corpus should satisfy a request.

title: VersionRAG: Version-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Evolving Documents
abstract: Explicitly represents document version sequences, content boundaries, and changes between versions, then routes queries through version-aware retrieval paths to prevent semantically relevant but temporally invalid document states from being conflated.

title: Regulatory Churn Evaluation Framework (RCEF): A Reproducible Methodology for Evaluating Retrieval Systems Under Document Evolution
abstract: Defines an evaluation methodology for retrieval over repositories affected by revision, supersession, expiration, and amendment, emphasizing that semantic relevance is insufficient when a document is invalid for the query's temporal or applicability conditions.

title: Archiving scientific data
abstract: Develops timestamp-based archival techniques for hierarchical scientific data that preserve historical versions and support retrieval of a specific prior state and its evolution over time.

title: Why and Where: A Characterization of Data Provenance
abstract: Distinguishes why-provenance from where-provenance and formalizes how derived information can be traced to the specific source data that contributed it, providing a foundation for evidence-object identity and derivation tracking.

title: Lineage tracing for general data warehouse transformations
abstract: Develops lineage tracing for derived warehouse data so that an output item can be mapped back to the concrete source items and transformations responsible for it.

title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations
abstract: Introduces ALCE for generating answers grounded in retrieved sources with explicit citations and evaluates whether cited evidence actually supports the corresponding generated claims, making concrete evidence provenance inspectable.

title: Document access in a multi-party information management system
abstract: Presents a sequencing access model for enterprise documents that represents who may retrieve a particular document version and when, tracks changing access privileges during workflows, and incorporates access-control information into secure retrieval indexes.

title: Secure search of private documents in an enterprise content management system
abstract: Integrates document access-control information with enterprise search indexing and query construction so that private organizational documents can be retrieved according to the requesting user's role and organizational context.

title: Access Rights in Enterprise Full-Text Search - Searching Large Intranets Effectively using Virtual Terms
abstract: Encodes access rights as virtual terms in an enterprise full-text index, integrating authorization constraints into retrieval rather than relying solely on expensive post-retrieval filtering.

title: Permission-Aware RAG: Identity and Access Management (IAM)-Based Access Filtering in Multi-Resource Environments
abstract: Enforces resource-level authorization during RAG by validating access in real time against the native IAM systems of independently governed sources, preserving their authorization boundaries instead of merging all policies into a common retrieval store.

title: Privacy-provisioned-permission-aware RAG in cloud using identity and access management, trust and large-language models (PPPARITL)
abstract: Introduces permission-aware RAG in which identity and access-management rules gate candidate evidence before ranking, with role-resource-action-condition authorization, trust assessment, and protected embeddings intended for enterprise cloud retrieval.
